Deficiencies in management of big
PSUs
*121. SHRI SANJAY RAUT:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether CAG has pointed out that
money spent by Government amounting
to Rs. 26,000 crores has not been accounted
for pointing to mammoth sloth and lack of
transparency in the functioning of PSUs

listed by CAG which include failure to

ANWARA TAIMUR:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) the authority which will credit the
taxpayers accounts within three days of an
assessment orders being sent to it in the
recently introduced scheme of Income-Tax
refund through SBI;
(b) how Government would avoid
inordinate delay in assessment process by
Income Tax officials;
(c) whether any study has been made
of the average time taken between the
receipt of the IT return and completion of
its assessment separately, individual,
Corporate Tax-payers-wise; and
(d) if so, what are the findings thereof?

Public Sector Undertakings Gas Authority

promote schemes like Medical Tourism,

Commonwealth Games in 2010;

plan; and

Hospitality Sector

in the luxury sector, the projected

ten cities;

be about 1.38 lakh jobs between

capable of producing about one lakh trained
personnel especially when only 20 per cent
of the hotel management graduates opt for
hospitality industry and balance attracted
towards BPOs, Airlines, Call Centres, etc.?

Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:

foreign exchange on the capital account

been taken or planned to curb speculative

Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased

(c) the response of Government

Floods in Bihar

MANDAL: Will the Minister of WATER
RESOURCES be pleased to state:
(a) the situation of floods in different
rivers in Bihar this year till date and the
losses suffered due to it;
(b) the preparations made for safety
and protection from flood and the amount
incurred thereon; and
(c) the view of Government for

Question 4326 given in the Rajya Sabha on

2006?

important observations with regard to PLR

Finance;

natural gas exploration

Direct flight from far East countries
to Delhi and Gaya
899. KUMARI NIRMALA
DESHPANDE: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that tourists and
pilgrims from the far East countries and
specially China are interested in visiting
India, but there are hardly any air
connections;
(b) if so, whether there is any plan to
connect Beijing, Shanghai, Taipeh and
Tokyo directly to Delhi and to Gaya to
facilitate the tourists and pilgrims; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Vision-2020
900. SHRI MANOHAR JOSHI:
SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) what are the salient features of the
Vision-2020 document prepared by his
Ministry for aviation sector;
(b) whether it is a fact that consolidation
of Indian aviation sector is taking place very
rapidly;
(c) whether the document has been
approved by Cabinet; and
(d) if so, what would be its impact on
the fares and passenger traffic?
Entry of Pawan Hans in regional
airline market
901. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
PSU Pawan Hans is exploring plans to
enter regional airline market with a fleet of
small fixed wing aircrafts that can seat about
20 passengers;
(b) if so, whether Government would
ensure that up-coming districts in  tribal
belt of Vidarbha, like Yavatmal, are given
first preference for introducing such a
service; and
(c) whether  subsidy is also given to
Pawan Hans if they find that the route is
not initially viable as is being done in North
East districts?

airlines
902. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:
Will the Minister of CIVIL  AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
formulated its much-awaited 'Civil Aviation
Policy' with a view to ease the norms for
launching overseas operations by domestic
airlines;
(b) if so, the details thereof indicating,
whether the Airports Authority of India is
likely to be restructured; and
(c) whether the new Policy would also
contain a 'Vision 2020' document that would
lay down a road map for aviation in the
light of recent boom in this sector in country

to promote 'merchant green-field airports'?

any suggestion regarding construction of

a meeting of industry representatives as

to promote 'Merchant Greenfield Airports'
as the Merchant Greenfield Airports will
be private airports built on private lands
within permissible civil aviation parameters
and air-traffic management regime;

meeting held; and

stressed the need to 'revisit' the policy on
airports as almost every airport expansion
project is facing problems over land
acquisition?

for commercial purpose under Airports
Authority of India;

earning profit and those running into loss;
(c) whether the Authority has decided
not to further develop the airports running
into loss; and
(d) if so, whether Birsa Munda Airport
at Ranchi, Jharkhand has been included
among such airports?

special treatment; and
(c) if so, the reasons therefor?
